items.title: Adversarial poetry as a universal single-turn jailbreak mechanism in LLMs
items.raw_content: We present evidence that adversarial poetry functions as a universal single-turn jailbreak technique for Large Language Models (LLMs). Across 25 frontier proprietary and open-weight models, curated poetic prompts yielded high attack-success rates (ASR), with some providers exceeding 90%. Mapping prompts to MLCommons and EU CoP risk taxonomies shows that poetic attacks transfer across CBRN, manipulation, cyber-offence, and loss-of-control domains. Converting 1,200 MLCommons harmful prompts into verse via a standardized meta-prompt produced ASRs up to 18 times higher than their prose baselines. Outputs are evaluated using an ensemble of 3 open-weight LLM judges, whose binary safety assessments were validated on a stratified human-labeled subset. items.title_zh: 对抗性诗歌作为大语言模型的通用单轮越狱手段
items.summary: Research presented in the paper finds that adversarial poetry acts as a universal single-turn jailbreak across 25 frontier proprietary and open-weight LLMs, with attack success exceeding 90% at some providers. Turning 1,200 harmful prompts into verse raised success rates by as much as 18 times compared with prose baselines.

items.title: Three Years from GPT-3 to Gemini 3
items.raw_content: I’ve been testing Google’s new Gemini 3 model. It is very good. But rather than give you benchmark numbers, I’m going to show you how far AI has come in three years by asking the AI to demonstrate it. It has been slightly less than three years since the release of ChatGPT. A few days before that launch, I wrote my first post on this Substack about OpenAI’s earlier GPT-3 model. Then ChatGPT came out, and I wrote immediately afterwards that “I am usually pretty hesitant to make technology predictions, but I think that this is going to change our world much sooner than we expect, and much more drastically. Rather than automating jobs that are repetitive & dangerous, there is now the prospect that the first jobs that are disrupted by AI will be more analytic; creative; and involve more writing and communication.”
items.title_zh: 从 GPT-3 到 Gemini 3 的三年
items.summary: The author says he has been testing Google's new Gemini 3 model and calls it very good. Rather than citing benchmark numbers, he uses the model to illustrate how far AI has progressed in the roughly three years since ChatGPT launched, recalling his earlier post on GPT-3.

items.title: Terence Tao: At the Erdos problem website, AI assistance now becoming routine
items.raw_content: Over at the Erdos problem website, AI assistance is now becoming routine. Here is what happened recently regarding Erdos problem #367 https://www.erdosproblems.com/367 : 1. On Nov 20, Wouter van Doorn produced a (human-generated) disproof of the second part of this problem, contingent on a congruence identity that he thought was true, and was "sure someoneone here is able to verify... does indeed hold". 2. A few hours later, I posed this problem to Gemini Deepthink, which (after about ten minutes) produced a complete proof of the identity (and confirmed the entire argument): https://gemini.google.com/share/81a65aecfd70 . The argument used some p-adic algebraic number theory which was overkill for this problem.
